title: Do tax cuts stimulate the economy? - Jonathan Smith
license: 字幕与元数据为本地构建产物；原视频版权归 YouTube 频道所有，播放通过官方嵌入，不下载视频文件。

blocks.en_text: When President Ronald Reagan began his first term in 1981,
blocks.zh_text: 1981年，罗纳德·里根总统开始他的第一个任期时，

blocks.en_text: the US economy was struggling.
blocks.zh_text: 美国经济正举步维艰。

blocks.en_text: Unemployment rates were high and getting higher,
blocks.zh_text: 失业率很高，而且还在不断攀升，

blocks.en_text: and in 1979, inflation had peaked at an all-time high for peacetime.
blocks.zh_text: 1979年，通货膨胀率达到了和平时期的最高点。

blocks.en_text: In an effort to combat these issues,
blocks.zh_text: 为了解决这些问题，

blocks.en_text: Reagan's administration introduced a number of economic policies,
blocks.zh_text: 里根政府推出了一系列经济政策，

blocks.en_text: including tax cuts for large corporations and high-income earners.
blocks.zh_text: 包括对大公司和高收入者减税。

blocks.en_text: The idea was that tax savings for the rich
blocks.zh_text: 其想法是，给富人的税收减免

blocks.en_text: would cause extra money to trickle down to everyone else,
blocks.zh_text: 会让多余的钱涓滴而下，惠及其他人，

blocks.en_text: and for that reason,
blocks.zh_text: 正因如此，

blocks.en_text: these policies are often referred to as trickle-down economics.
blocks.zh_text: 这些政策常被称为涓滴经济学。

blocks.en_text: From the 80s to the late 90s,
blocks.zh_text: 从80年代到90年代末，

blocks.en_text: the US saw one of its longest and strongest periods
blocks.zh_text: 美国经历了历史上最长、最强劲的

blocks.en_text: of economic growth in history.
blocks.zh_text: 经济增长时期之一。

blocks.en_text: Median income rose, as did rates of job creation.
blocks.zh_text: 收入中位数上升了，就业创造率也提高了。

blocks.en_text: Since then, many politicians have invoked trickle-down theory
blocks.zh_text: 从那以后，许多政客都援引涓滴理论

blocks.en_text: as a justification for tax cuts—
blocks.zh_text: 作为减税的理由——

blocks.en_text: but did these policies actually work,
blocks.zh_text: 但这些政策真的奏效了吗？

blocks.en_text: either in the sense of stimulating economic growth,
blocks.zh_text: 无论是从刺激经济增长的意义上说，

blocks.en_text: or in terms of improving circumstances for Americans?
blocks.zh_text: 还是从改善美国人生活状况的角度说？

blocks.en_text: Would they work in other circumstances?
blocks.zh_text: 它们在别的情况下会奏效吗？

blocks.en_text: To answer these questions,
blocks.zh_text: 要回答这些问题，

blocks.en_text: the main things to consider are whether the impact of the tax cut
blocks.zh_text: 主要需要考虑的是：减税对政府税收的影响

blocks.en_text: on the government’s tax revenue is harmful,
blocks.zh_text: 是否有害，

blocks.en_text: whether the money saved in taxes actually stimulates the economy,
blocks.zh_text: 省下来的税款是否真的刺激了经济，

blocks.en_text: and whether stimulating the economy actually improves people’s lives.
blocks.zh_text: 以及刺激经济是否真的改善了人们的生活。

blocks.en_text: The idea behind tax cuts is that if taxes are too high,
blocks.zh_text: 减税背后的想法是，如果税率太高，

blocks.en_text: people will be less willing to work,
blocks.zh_text: 人们就不太愿意工作，

blocks.en_text: which would ultimately decrease tax revenue.
blocks.zh_text: 这最终会减少税收。

blocks.en_text: So at a lower tax rate, the government might actually gain more tax money
blocks.zh_text: 所以在较低的税率下，政府实际上可能获得更多的税收，

blocks.en_text: that it can theoretically put towards improving life for its citizens,
blocks.zh_text: 理论上可以用来改善公民的生活，

blocks.en_text: because people will work more when they get to keep more of their earnings.
blocks.zh_text: 因为当人们能留下更多收入时，他们就会更努力地工作。

blocks.en_text: Of course, there’s a limit to how much the government can cut taxes:
blocks.zh_text: 当然，政府能减多少税是有限度的：

blocks.en_text: at a zero tax rate there is no tax revenue regardless of how much people are working.
blocks.zh_text: 在零税率下，无论人们工作多少，都没有税收。

blocks.en_text: So while cuts from a very high tax rate might be fine,
blocks.zh_text: 所以，从很高的税率往下减也许没问题，

blocks.en_text: cuts from a lower tax rate might be counterproductive,
blocks.zh_text: 但从较低的税率往下减可能适得其反，

blocks.en_text: hampering the government's ability to accomplish crucial things.
blocks.zh_text: 削弱政府完成关键事务的能力。

blocks.en_text: Tax rates were extremely high when Reagan took office.
blocks.zh_text: 里根上任时，税率极高。

blocks.en_text: His administration cut the highest income tax bracket from 70% to 28%
blocks.zh_text: 他的政府把最高所得税税率从70%降到28%，

blocks.en_text: and corporation tax from 48% to 34%.
blocks.zh_text: 把公司税从48%降到34%。

blocks.en_text: By comparison, as of early 2021,
blocks.zh_text: 相比之下，截至2021年初，

blocks.en_text: those rates were 37% and 21% respectively.
blocks.zh_text: 这两个税率分别是37%和21%。

blocks.en_text: When tax rates are lower, tax cuts for the wealthy can be harmful.
blocks.zh_text: 当税率较低时，给富人减税反而可能有害。

blocks.en_text: For example, in 2012 to 2013,
lawmakers cut the top tax-rate in the state of Kansas by almost 30%
blocks.zh_text: 立法者把堪萨斯州的最高税率下调了近30%，

blocks.en_text: and reduced some business tax rates to zero.
blocks.zh_text: 还把一些企业税率降到了零。

blocks.en_text: As a result, the government’s balance sheet immediately fell
blocks.zh_text: 结果，政府的资产负债表立刻

blocks.en_text: into negative territory and did not recover,
blocks.zh_text: 陷入负值，而且再也没能恢复，

blocks.en_text: implying that wealthy individuals and companies did not invest
blocks.zh_text: 这意味着富人和企业并没有把钱

blocks.en_text: back into the economy.
blocks.zh_text: 重新投回经济中去。

blocks.en_text: In short, the money did not trickle down.
blocks.zh_text: 简而言之，钱并没有往下渗透。

blocks.en_text: This appears to be a trend:
blocks.zh_text: 这似乎是一种趋势：

blocks.en_text: in a study over multiple periods of history and across 18 countries,
blocks.zh_text: 在一项跨越历史上多个时期、涵盖18个国家的研究中，

blocks.en_text: The London School of Economics found that cutting taxes
blocks.zh_text: 伦敦政治经济学院发现，减税

blocks.en_text: increased the wealth of the top 1% of people,
blocks.zh_text: 增加了最富有的1%人群的财富，

blocks.en_text: but had little effect on the economy as a whole.
blocks.zh_text: 但对整体经济几乎没有影响。

blocks.en_text: In order for tax cuts for the rich to truly stimulate the economy,
blocks.zh_text: 要让给富人减税真正刺激经济，

blocks.en_text: they would have to spend the saved money
blocks.zh_text: 他们就得把省下来的钱花出去，

blocks.en_text: putting it back into, for example, local businesses—
blocks.zh_text: 比如重新投入到本地企业中去——

blocks.en_text: but this isn’t what happens in practice.
blocks.zh_text: 但实际情况并非如此。

blocks.en_text: No economic policy operates in isolation:
blocks.zh_text: 没有哪项经济政策是孤立运作的：

blocks.en_text: each time and place is unique with multiple policies in place simultaneously,
blocks.zh_text: 每个时间、每个地点都是独特的，同时有多项政策在起作用，

blocks.en_text: so there is only ever one test case for each set of scenarios.
blocks.zh_text: 所以每一组情形都只有一次试验机会。

blocks.en_text: This makes it difficult to deliver definitive rulings on whether
blocks.zh_text: 这就很难给出确定的结论，来判断

blocks.en_text: an economic policy worked,
blocks.zh_text: 某项经济政策是否奏效，

blocks.en_text: whether something else might have worked better,
blocks.zh_text: 别的做法是否可能效果更好，

blocks.en_text: or whether it would work in a different situation.
blocks.zh_text: 或者它在另一种情况下是否也行得通。

blocks.en_text: And yet, rhetoric around trickle-down economics,
blocks.zh_text: 然而，围绕涓滴经济学的那些说法，

blocks.en_text: both during the Reagan era and since,
blocks.zh_text: 无论是在里根时代还是在那之后，

blocks.en_text: often promises something definitive:
blocks.zh_text: 往往都承诺得很绝对：

blocks.en_text: that spending by society’s richest members on things other than taxes
blocks.zh_text: 说社会最富有的成员在纳税之外的花费，

blocks.en_text: directly improves the financial circumstances of the less wealthy.
blocks.zh_text: 会直接改善不那么富裕的人的财务状况。

blocks.en_text: And there’s not much evidence to support that.
blocks.zh_text: 而支持这一点的证据并不多。
